hints: Notice the conditions, NaOH in ethanol causes elimination of HBr, and here two HBr molecules must be lost to go from C5H10Br2 to C5H8.
Draw BrCH2CH2CH2CHBrCH3 and see where double bonds can form, the Br on C1 can only give a C1=C2 bond, while the Br on C4 can give C3=C4 or C4=C5.
Check each diene for E/Z isomerism by looking for a C=C with two different groups on each carbon, then count the distinct stereoisomers.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

NaOH in ethanol is the classic condition for dehydrohalogenation by elimination. Since we start with a dibromide, two molecules of HBr are eliminated.

$$\text{BrCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHBrCH}_3 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_5\text{H}_8 + 2\text{NaBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Find where the double bonds must form**

The Br on C1 has H neighbours only on C2, so the first double bond must be C1=C2. The Br on C4 has H neighbours on both C3 and C5, so the second double bond can be C3=C4 or C4=C5.

**Draw the two structural dienes**

This gives two structural isomers, both dienes which are still classed as alkenes:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \text{ (penta-1,3-diene)}$$ 
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \text{ (penta-1,4-diene)}$$

**Count stereoisomers**

Penta-1,4-diene has two terminal $\text{C}=\text{C}$ bonds with two H atoms on the end carbons, so no E/Z isomerism. Penta-1,3-diene has an internal $\text{C3}=\text{C4}$ bond with H and $\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$ on C3, and H and $\text{CH}_3$ on C4, so it exists as E and Z forms. Total distinct alkenes = 2 + 1 = 3.

options.A: 1 is too low because it ignores that the second elimination has two different positions and ignores stereoisomerism. Both penta-1,3-diene and penta-1,4-diene can form.
options.B: 2 counts the two structural dienes correctly but forgets stereoisomerism. Penta-1,3-diene shows cis-trans (E/Z) isomerism at the C3=C4 bond, adding one more isomer.
options.C: 3 is correct: penta-1,4-diene gives 1 isomer and penta-1,3-diene gives E and Z isomers, making 3 distinct isomeric alkenes of formula C5H8 in total.
options.D: 4 is too high. It would require an extra structural or stereoisomer, for example wrongly counting E/Z for penta-1,4-diene, which cannot show it, or inventing a branched or cumulated diene that cannot form directly by elimination here.
